newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ramped up in busy Thursday dealings on perceptions the heavy selling, which has wiped almost three percent off the market's value this month, was overdone.

Dealers said buyers were lured into the market during the morning when it became evident futures players, who have been responsible for large-volume arbitrage sales, were keeping largely to the sidelines.
"The market had to bounce. It had been sold down for over seven consecutive days. It is a case of the things being overdone," a dealer said.
They said prices had been depressed artificially by basket sales.
"There has been some buying interest all along from institutions but they have been very selective. Without the futures operators in today, they got a lot more aggressive," a dealer said.
Perceptions amongst economists that there would not be a hike in interest rates until next year also boosted the market.
Economists told Reuters on Thursday Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals was likely to hold the key rate at 16 percent pending further signals on money supply and the balance of payments.
Foreigners who had been largely absent in the past few days, were seen hunting stock.
The overall index ended 60.6 points firmer at 6,815.9 supported by the industrial index which rose 66.1 points to 7,980.2.
Amongst stocks, Anglo put on 75 cents to 269.25 rand, Nedcor was up 225 cents to 67 rand and Amic jumped 350 cents to 161 rand.
Gold stocks jumped for the first time in many sessions, initially boosted by bullion's climb above the $383 level on Wednesday night.
Although bullion had since slipped back to around $382.75 before close of the local market the buying spree continued helped by overnight gains in South African gold stocks listed in U.S.
The index ended up 31.7 points at 1,743.6, with heavyweight Vaal Reefs adding 850 cents to 361 rand, Freegold up 120 cents to 42.70 and Loraine gaining 30 cents to 15 rand.
Gains on both gold and industrial boards added 60.6 points to the overall index which finished at 6,815.9.
Dealers said the market was expected to continue firmer on Friday, although it would depend if futures players entered the market.
On the futures market contracts headed higher in late trade boosted by Wall Street's fifth consecutive high overnight and gains on the spot market.
The December industrial index contract was last at 7,670/80 from 7,546, the gold index contract at 1,235/45 from 1,224 and the all-share steady at 6,128.
